design_detail: Completed systematic review with random-effects meta-analysis (not a protocol) of placebo-controlled parallel-group randomized trials of 'psychostimulants' (classical stimulants dexamphetamine and methylphenidate, plus bupropion and modafinil) for amphetamine or methamphetamine use disorder in people aged 14 or older. Searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Cochrane CENTRAL and CINAHL to August 2016 without language limits. 17 trials (1387 participants) included; end-of-treatment abstinence pooled from 5 trials and retention from 14 (odds ratios, RevMan 5.3); Cochrane risk-of-bias tool in duplicate; GRADE. Methods set in an unpublished a priori protocol; PROSPERO registration was submitted but not accepted.
can_establish: That, in trials published to August 2016, bupropion and modafinil (the only drugs in the abstinence analysis) did not increase urine-verified abstinence in the final 2 weeks of treatment, and that the four drugs together did not detectably improve retention to the end of trials; with very low certainty for both.
cannot_establish: Whether the classical stimulant agonists (dexamphetamine, methylphenidate) affect abstinence, because none of their trials entered the abstinence meta-analysis; whether any drug is harmful or safe (adverse events were not analysed quantitatively and denominators are not given); or whether longer treatment improves retention (a subgroup of two trials, one in incarcerated men).

sample.recruitment: Not applicable at review level. Trials from the USA (10), Sweden (2), Australia (2), Iran (1), Finland (1) and Finland with New Zealand (1), per Table 1 (editors' count); populations included adults with any frequency of use, people using less than daily, one adolescent trial, men who have sex with men, people with ADHD (one trial in incarcerated men) and people who inject.
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Included: randomized controlled trials comparing any psychostimulant with an inactive control (placebo) in people aged 14 or older with a DSM diagnosis of amphetamine or methamphetamine use disorder (abuse or dependence), or DSM-5 stimulant use disorder with amphetamine or methamphetamine data extractable. Excluded: non-randomized or quasi-randomized designs, cocaine-only trials, trials managing withdrawal rather than dependence, and laboratory administration studies with non-substance outcomes. Psychostimulants identified from the ATC and AHFS classifications following earlier Cochrane reviews, including bupropion and modafinil (Methods › Inclusion and exclusion criteria).
sample.demographics: Table 1 gives per-trial n, percentage men (47.4% to 100%) and mean ages (17.5 to 42 years). Two trials enrolled only men (one of men who have sex with men, one of incarcerated men with ADHD); one trial was in adolescents; three trials restricted entry to non-daily or low-frequency use.
sample.attrition: Not applicable at review level. The review reports that most trials lost more than half of participants before completion; in the retention meta-analysis 332 of 626 (53.0%) on psychostimulants and 268 of 558 (48.0%) on placebo completed (Table 2).
sample.selection_effects: Trials are small (47% had 30 or fewer participants per arm) and many excluded people with other substance use disorders. The five trials in the abstinence analysis were all of methamphetamine dependence and tested only bupropion (3) or modafinil (2).

exposure.measurement: The exposure is the assigned medication, as study conditions (Table 1): modafinil 200 or 400 mg daily (3 trials); bupropion 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg daily (6 trials); methylphenidate up to 54, 72 or 180 mg daily (6 trials); dexamphetamine 60 mg daily or titrated to a maximum of 110 mg daily (2 trials). Treatment periods 8 to 24 weeks.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only, as above. A planned dose subgroup analysis was not possible because doses were similar within each drug.
exposure.polysubstance: Many trials excluded comorbid substance use disorders (references 13, 24 to 26, 28 to 30, 33, 35), which the review treats as indirectness.

comparison.controls: Inactive placebo in all 17 trials; the placebo substance was reported in three (lactose in two, gelatin in one).
comparison.matching: Not applicable (randomized trials). Random sequence generation was adequately reported in fewer than half of trials and allocation concealment was not adequately reported in over 75% (80% in the GRADE footnote).
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Same populations as the active arms.

outcomes.instruments: Primary: (1) abstinence, as the proportion of participants with methamphetamine-free urine tests over the longest substance-free period assessed across trials, which in the five pooled trials was the final 2 weeks of treatment ('terminal abstinence'); (2) retention, as the proportion remaining in treatment at the end of the trial. Secondary: serious adverse events, defined as any event causing hospitalization or dropout.
outcomes.validity_norms: Urinalysis is objective; retention is a process measure whose meaning depends on trial context (one trial enrolled incarcerated men, in whom the authors note expectations about parole may have affected retention).
outcomes.operationalization: Benefit is a higher odds of terminal urine-verified abstinence or of trial completion with medication than with placebo. Harm was to be the incidence of serious adverse events, but these were only described qualitatively.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None. 8 counts the two primary pooled estimates and the six tests for subgroup differences (abstinence by drug and by use frequency; retention by diagnosis, drug, use frequency and treatment duration), which together produced 14 subgroup estimates. The only significant result (retention with treatment longer than 12 weeks; subgroup difference p = 0.05) emerged from this set.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not applicable at review level. Screening, full-text review (kappa 0.84), extraction and risk-of-bias assessment (kappa 0.83) were done independently by two reviewers.

analysis.effect_sizes: Random-effects, inverse-variance odds ratios. Abstinence (5 trials, 642 participants: 70 of 353 on medication, 19.8%, versus 62 of 289 on placebo, 21.5%): OR 0.97 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.45), p = 0.87, I2 2%; GRADE very low; absolute effect 5 fewer per 1000 (64 fewer to 69 more). Editors' calculation from the pooled counts (crude, not stratified by trial): risk difference -1.6 percentage points (95% CI -7.9 to 4.7). Subgroups: modafinil OR 0.86 (0.46 to 1.61), I2 0%; bupropion OR 1.12 (0.54 to 2.33), I2 47%; difference p = 0.59; non-daily use OR 1.24 (0.34 to 4.48), I2 74%; unspecified frequency OR 0.92 (0.54 to 1.54); difference p = 0.67. Retention (14 trials, 1184 participants: 332 of 626, 53.0%, versus 268 of 558, 48.0%): OR 1.20 (0.91 to 1.58), I2 15%; GRADE very low; 46 more per 1000 (23 fewer to 113 more). Editors' calculation: crude risk difference 5.0 percentage points (-0.7 to 10.7). Retention subgroups: amphetamine use disorder OR 1.54 (0.48 to 4.99), I2 57%; methamphetamine use disorder OR 1.11 (0.86 to 1.44), I2 0%; dexamphetamine OR 2.50 (0.80 to 7.87), p = 0.12; treatment longer than 12 weeks (2 trials) OR 2.45 (1.14 to 5.25), p = 0.02, subgroup difference chi-square 3.93, df 1, p = 0.05.
analysis.preregistration_detail: The paper states the methods were set a priori in an unpublished protocol available on request, and that PROSPERO registration was submitted but did not meet eligibility at the time. The protocol was not seen, so adherence to it cannot be checked; one planned subgroup analysis (dose) was abandoned and three (age, diagnosis, duration) could not be run for abstinence.
analysis.selective_reporting: Sensitivity analyses (removing special populations and removing trials at high risk for selective reporting or incomplete outcome data) are reported only as not changing the results, without numbers. Serious adverse events are reported as counts of dropouts without denominators. The review used published data only and did not seek unpublished outcome data.
analysis.power: Not addressed formally. The abstinence analysis has 642 participants and about 132 events; its interval (OR 0.65 to 1.45; roughly 6 percentage points either way) does not exclude a modest benefit or harm.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Across five trials of bupropion or modafinil, about one in five participants on either medication or placebo had urine-verified abstinence in the last 2 weeks of treatment, with no difference (OR 0.97). Across 14 trials of four drugs, about half completed, with a non-significant 5-point difference favouring medication (OR 1.20). Certainty was very low for both. Of the five planned retention subgroup contrasts, only treatment duration was borderline (p = 0.05), with OR 2.45 in two trials longer than 12 weeks. Several individual methylphenidate trials reported fewer positive urines (Table 1), but none contributed to the pooled abstinence estimate.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract and conclusions state that psychostimulants had no effect on sustained abstinence or retention. For abstinence this generalizes from bupropion and modafinil to the whole class: no dexamphetamine or methylphenidate trial was in that analysis, which the abstract does not say. The conclusions also state that longer treatment may favour retention, which rests on two trials, a borderline subgroup difference among several subgroup tests, and a trial-classification problem (see reporting issues); the Discussion itself calls the finding non-generalizable. The abstract's statement that serious adverse events did not differ between groups rests on qualitative reports and dropout counts without denominators. The overall conclusion of very low certainty and the call for standardized outcomes are well supported.

timeline.event: Pérez-Mañá et al., Cochrane review and meta-analysis of psychostimulants for amphetamine abuse or dependence, which found no effect (cited as reference 7; this review updates it).
This review: 17 trials to August 2016; no pooled effect on terminal abstinence (5 trials) or retention (14 trials).

Siefried et al., narrative systematic review of all medications to June 2019 (43 trials); includes 14 of this review's 17 trials but not Das 2010 or the two Konstenius methylphenidate trials, and describes the Ling 2014 methylphenidate trial and the Elkashef 2008 bupropion trial differently (no urine difference; 156 rather than 151 participants).

replication.where_it_stands: The abstinence result is a statement about bupropion and modafinil, consistent with the null primary results of those trials as summarized by Siefried et al. (2020). Whether classical stimulant agonists improve abstinence was not answered by this review and remained open in the later reviews read for the encyclopedia. The overlap with Pérez-Mañá et al. (2013) and Siefried et al. (2020) means these reviews are not independent replications.

funding.funder: Population Genomics Program and the Peter Boris Centre for Addictions Research (McMaster University and St Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton); the senior author is supported by a Hamilton Academic Health Sciences Organization Innovation Grant. The funders are stated to have had no role in design, review, analysis, interpretation or reporting.
funding.declared_conflicts: The authors declare no competing interests.
funding.affiliations_note: Authors from McMaster University (Clinical Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Neuroscience, Medicine, Health Sciences Library), St Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton, Hamilton Health Sciences and St George's University of London. None of the authors appears among the authors of the included trials listed in the references.

what_would_settle_it: Adequately powered placebo-controlled trials of classical stimulant agonists (dexamphetamine or lisdexamfetamine, methylphenidate) in people with moderate to severe methamphetamine use disorder, using a common responder outcome (urine-verified abstinence or a prespecified reduction over the last weeks of treatment) and treatment of more than 12 weeks, with systematic adverse-event reporting; or an individual-participant-data meta-analysis of the existing trials using one outcome definition.

domains.domain: 1. PICO components in research question and inclusion criteria
domains.note: Population, interventions, placebo comparator and outcomes specified.
An a priori protocol is stated to exist (unpublished, available on request); PROSPERO registration was submitted but not accepted; deviations (abandoned dose subgroup) are explained.
Restriction to randomized trials is stated without rationale.

Five databases from inception to August 2016 with a strategy developed with a health-sciences librarian (in an additional file), no language or date limits, reference lists of past reviews and included trials hand-searched, ClinicalTrials.gov searched for unpublished and ongoing trials; no other grey literature and no expert contact, and published data only. The search ended in August 2016 and the article was published on 14 November 2016; the saved full text has no submission date, so the interval to submission cannot be stated.
Two reviewers independently; kappa 0.84 at full text.
Two authors with a pilot-tested form.

domains.domain: 7. List of excluded studies with justification (critical)
domains.note: No list of excluded full texts in the article or among the three additional files described (PRISMA checklist, search strategy, extraction form).

domains.domain: 8. Included studies described in adequate detail
domains.note: Table 1 gives diagnosis and population, length, drug and dose, n, sex, age and each trial's substance-use result.

domains.domain: 9. Satisfactory risk-of-bias assessment of included studies (critical)
domains.note: Cochrane risk-of-bias tool, in duplicate (kappa 0.83); per-trial judgments in Figures 2 and 3 (images).

domains.domain: 10. Funding sources of included studies reported
domains.note: Only a general statement that most trials were not industry funded.

AMSTAR 2 item 11 is yes or no for randomized trials. Judged yes: the review gives a rationale for pooling psychostimulants as a class (agents sharing a dopaminergic mechanism with the drugs used, Background; a published classification approach, Inclusion criteria), pools with random-effects inverse-variance weighting, reports I2 with a stated threshold, and investigates heterogeneity through a priori subgroup analyses. Two caveats that do not make the methods inappropriate: the class pooling puts four pharmacologically different drugs in one estimate, which the review itself carries as GRADE indirectness; and the exclusion of the 151-participant bupropion trial (Elkashef 2008) from the retention analysis follows a prespecified rule (of trials with overlapping participants, keep the larger, Methods › Data synthesis; Anderson 2015 had 204), but the overlap itself is asserted and never explained (reporting issue 1).

domains.domain: 12. Impact of risk of bias on pooled results assessed
domains.note: AMSTAR 2 item 12 is yes, no or no meta-analysis. Judged yes: sensitivity analyses were run removing trials at high risk of bias for selective outcome reporting and for incomplete outcome data, one at a time, for both pooled outcomes (Results › Sensitivity analyses). Only the conclusion is given (estimates did not change appreciably) and no numbers are reported, which limits what a reader can check but does not mean the impact was not assessed.

domains.domain: 13. Risk of bias accounted for in interpretation (critical)
domains.note: GRADE very low for both outcomes, with risk of bias, indirectness and imprecision discussed.
Prespecified subgroup analyses and discussion; but see the reporting issue on overlapping intervals.
Funnel plots for both outcomes, visually symmetrical and discussed; with five trials for abstinence the plot cannot detect asymmetry, which the review does not acknowledge.

domains.domain: 16. Conflicts of interest and funding reported
domains.note: Funding and absence of competing interests declared.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: AMSTAR 2 critical items here are 2, 4, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 15. After the second reading, one critical item is answered no (item 7, no list of excluded full texts) and two critical items are partly met (item 2, an unpublished protocol with a PROSPERO submission that was not accepted; item 4, a search without grey literature or expert contact), with non-critical weaknesses at items 3 and 10. Under AMSTAR 2 one critical flaw, with or without non-critical weaknesses, gives low confidence, so the overall rating stays low confidence after items 11 and 12 were changed from an unavailable response to yes. The review is otherwise well conducted (duplicate screening, extraction and risk-of-bias rating with kappas reported, the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool, GRADE with absolute effects, funnel plots for both outcomes), and its null pooled estimates are credible for the drugs that entered them. The main limitation for the encyclopedia is scope, not bias: the abstinence estimate covers bupropion and modafinil only, and the one significant subgroup estimate rests on two trials.

key_findings.finding: 17 placebo-controlled parallel-group trials (1387 participants) were included: bupropion 6, methylphenidate 6, modafinil 3, dexamphetamine 2; after screening 1251 unique citations.

End-of-treatment abstinence (urine-verified, final 2 weeks), 5 trials of bupropion or modafinil in methamphetamine dependence: 70 of 353 (19.8%) on medication versus 62 of 289 (21.5%) on placebo; OR 0.97 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.45), p = 0.87, I2 2%; 5 fewer per 1000 (64 fewer to 69 more); GRADE very low.
key_findings.locator: Results › Meta-analyses: abstinence; Figure 4a; Table 2; Table 3
key_findings.note: Editors' crude risk difference from the pooled counts: -1.6 percentage points (95% CI -7.9 to 4.7). No dexamphetamine or methylphenidate trial contributed.

key_findings.finding: Abstinence subgroups: modafinil OR 0.86 (0.46 to 1.61), bupropion OR 1.12 (0.54 to 2.33), subgroup difference p = 0.59; non-daily use OR 1.24 (0.34 to 4.48, I2 74%), unspecified frequency OR 0.92 (0.54 to 1.54), difference p = 0.67.
Retention to end of trial, 14 trials: 332 of 626 (53.0%) on medication versus 268 of 558 (48.0%) on placebo; OR 1.20 (0.91 to 1.58), I2 15%; 46 more per 1000 (23 fewer to 113 more); GRADE very low.
key_findings.locator: Results › Meta-analyses: retention; Figure 5a; Tables 2 and 3
key_findings.note: Editors' crude risk difference: 5.0 percentage points (-0.7 to 10.7).

key_findings.finding: Retention subgroups: amphetamine use disorder OR 1.54 (0.48 to 4.99), methamphetamine use disorder OR 1.11 (0.86 to 1.44); no drug subgroup significant (dexamphetamine, 2 trials, OR 2.50, 0.80 to 7.87); treatment longer than 12 weeks, 2 trials, OR 2.45 (1.14 to 5.25), p = 0.02, subgroup difference p = 0.05.
key_findings.locator: Results › Subgroup analyses (retention); Figure 5b to 5e; Discussion, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Individual trial results as tabulated: methylphenidate trials reporting fewer positive urines than placebo (Tiihonen 2007 OR 0.42, 0.24 to 0.72; Ling 2014 OR 0.18 at week 14, p = 0.025; Rezaei 2015 at week 10, p = 0.03; Konstenius 2014, 23% versus 16% negative urines, p = 0.047) did not enter the abstinence meta-analysis; the adolescent bupropion trial favoured placebo (5.0 versus 8.9 negative screens, p = 0.043).

Risk of bias (Cochrane tool): random sequence generation adequately reported in fewer than half of trials; allocation concealment inadequately reported in over 75%; 16 of 17 blinded participants and personnel; all unclear or high risk for blinding of outcome assessment; high risk for incomplete outcome data in half of trials; 47% of trials had 30 or fewer participants per arm.
key_findings.locator: Results › Risk of bias assessment; Discussion, 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: Safety: only 3 of 17 trials used a standardized adverse-event instrument; dropouts attributed to serious adverse events were 8 (modafinil), 11 (bupropion) and 7 (methylphenidate) against 11 on placebo, without denominators; no trial attributed serious events to study medication.

Sensitivity analyses removing trials in specific populations (men who have sex with men; ADHD; incarcerated men with ADHD) or trials at high risk for selective reporting or incomplete outcome data did not change either primary result (numbers not shown); funnel plots showed no visible asymmetry.
key_findings.locator: Results › Sensitivity analyses; Publication bias; Figure 6

reporting_issues.issue: The 'longer than 12 weeks' retention subgroup contains two trials (references 26 and 28), but Table 1 gives study lengths over 12 weeks for ten trials (for example Shearer 2009, 22 weeks; Anderson 2012, 16 weeks), and the Description of studies names references 25, 28 and 32 as the trials with 20 to 24 weeks of treatment, while Table 1 gives reference 25 a length of 13 weeks and reference 26 a length of 24 weeks.
reporting_issues.consequence: The classification behind the only significant subgroup result (OR 2.45) cannot be reproduced from the paper; the duration finding should not be cited without the primary trials' treatment periods.

reporting_issues.issue: The bupropion trial by Elkashef et al. (2008; 151 participants, 18 weeks) is excluded from the retention meta-analysis for an 'overlapping sample' with Anderson et al. (2015; 204 people using less than daily, 12 weeks), with no explanation; the two trials differ in size, duration and eligibility in Table 1, and Siefried et al. (2020) list them as separate trials.
reporting_issues.consequence: A sizeable bupropion trial may have been omitted from the retention estimate without justification; its direction of effect is unknown here.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion states that individual trial odds ratios showed little to no overlap of confidence intervals, and GRADE downgrades both outcomes for inconsistency, while the pooled analyses report I2 of 2% (abstinence) and 15% (retention).
reporting_issues.consequence: The inconsistency downgrade and the description of non-overlapping intervals are not supported by the reported heterogeneity statistics; the very low rating is driven mainly by risk of bias, indirectness and imprecision.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract states that the incidence of serious adverse events did not differ between groups, but no incidence was calculated: the review reports only counts of dropouts attributed to serious events (26 across medication arms, 11 on placebo) without denominators.
reporting_issues.consequence: The review provides no quantitative evidence on safety; a claim of no difference in serious adverse events cannot rest on it.

reporting_issues.issue: The publication-bias section introduces both funnel plots as being for treatment retention, then describes Figure 6a as built from the five abstinence trials; and it argues the abstinence plot would stay symmetrical if other trials were added.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor drafting error; a funnel plot of five trials cannot assess publication bias, so this domain is effectively unassessed for abstinence.

reporting_issues.issue: The text says drug subgroups in the retention analysis contained two to six trials, but after the stated exclusions (references 22, 32 and 33) the largest drug subgroup (methylphenidate) can contain at most five of the 14 trials (editors' count from Table 1).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; suggests the subgroup composition was not reported exactly.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC5109734 (all sections, Tables 1 to 3 rendered as text, funding, contributions, competing interests and reference list read; Figures 1 to 6 (PRISMA flow, risk-of-bias graphs, forest plots, funnel plots) are images and their values were not extracted beyond what the text states; Additional files 1 to 3 not read).

disagreements.reviewer: 'partial yes' is not an AMSTAR 2 response for item 11; on the instrument's criteria the item would be 'yes', or 'no' if the editors treat the unexplained exclusion of Elkashef 2008 as an inappropriate method
disagreements.resolution: Changed to yes. AMSTAR 2 offers partial yes only for items 2, 4, 7, 8 and 9 (METHODS §5.3), so the first-pass response was not available for this item. Decided from the source: item 11 asks for a justification for combining, an appropriate weighted technique and investigation of heterogeneity, and the review does all three (Background and Inclusion criteria for the class rationale; random-effects inverse variance with I2; prespecified subgroup analyses explicitly run to explore heterogeneity). The Elkashef 2008 exclusion follows the prespecified larger-sample rule in Methods › Data synthesis rather than an ad hoc choice, so it is a reporting gap (already reporting issue 1), not an inappropriate method. Item 11 is critical, so this changes the count of critical flaws.

disagreements.reviewer: 'partial yes' is not an AMSTAR 2 response for item 12; the item would be 'yes', since sensitivity analyses removing high-risk trials were run, though reported without numbers
disagreements.resolution: Changed to yes. Checked at Results › Sensitivity analyses: trials at high risk for selective outcome reporting and for incomplete outcome data were removed one at a time for both primary outcomes and the pooled estimates are reported as unchanged. The missing numbers are a reporting weakness, kept in the note; item 12 is not a critical item, so the overall rating is unaffected.

disagreements.reviewer: the claim that the search ended within 3 months of submission could not be checked: the article-notes panel with the submission date is not in the saved text
disagreements.resolution: Reworded to what the source shows: search to August 2016, publication 14 November 2016 (the journal line in the saved page). The judgment 'partial yes' is unchanged, since it rests on the absence of grey literature and expert contact, not on the date.

disagreements.first_pass: low-confidence (from one critical no and three partly met items)
disagreements.reviewer: agrees with low confidence; notes that treating item 11 as a critical no would give critically low
disagreements.resolution: Overall recomputed under the AMSTAR 2 critical-item rule after items 11 and 12 were decided from the source: critical items 2 and 4 partly met, 7 no, 9, 11, 13 and 15 yes. One critical flaw with non-critical weaknesses gives low confidence, so low-confidence stands; the reasoning now states the count.

disagreements.reviewer: recounted from the Results as 14 (abstinence by drug 2 and by frequency 2; retention by diagnosis 2, by drug 4, by frequency 2, by duration 2)
disagreements.resolution: Corrected to 14. Recounted independently from the Results: abstinence by medication 2 (modafinil, bupropion) and by use frequency 2; retention by diagnosis 2, by medication 4 (the subgroup-difference test has 3 degrees of freedom), by use frequency 2 and by treatment duration 2. The six subgroup-difference tests and the statement that only the longer-than-12-weeks retention estimate reached significance are both right.
